question: Should automatic Codex tool summaries continue to honor Slack’s documented `streaming.preview.toolProgress` preference, or should Slack always convert or suppress them regardless of that setting?
rationale: The PR changes a documented user preference and selects a permanent cross-plugin ownership boundary, so implementation correctness alone cannot establish the intended product contract.

options.title: Preserve configured progress
options.body: Route summaries through the canonical typed progress pipeline and suppress them only when Slack’s resolved configuration requests suppression.

options.title: Always suppress summaries
options.body: Declare automatic summaries non-deliverable chrome, then intentionally update the documented contract, upgrade expectations, tests, and live proof.

options.title: Pause this approach
options.body: Keep the existing canonical progress behavior and close or redesign this PR if the accidental-send case cannot be fixed without a competing payload channel.

recommendation.title: Preserve configured progress
recommendation.body: Route summaries through the canonical typed progress pipeline and suppress them only when Slack’s resolved configuration requests suppression.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows the strongest direct ownership of the existing tool-progress safety behavior and its merge decisions.
